bib.title: Agentic Discovery of Neural Architectures: AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Agentic Discovery of Neural Architectures: AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design", Pepe, Lin, Magka, Acun, Foster, Wu, Protopopov, Wu, Bachrach (FAIR at Meta). arXiv 2605.15871v2, dated Oct 2026. Preprint.

COVERAGE: The PDF has 55 pages and the extraction is 194,896 chars. I read the main text in full (abstract, sections 1-7, limitations, about 76,000 chars). I read the appendix text selectively: A (related work), B headings, C captions, D aggregation list, G (full text, Tables 19-21) and the start of H. Appendices B-F are mostly tables, data labels and per-model numbers. I did not read the references or the Appendix H code listing line by line. pypdf warned "Exceeded 5000 form XObject invocations... further form content is skipped", so some figure-embedded text may be missing. The text I did read was intact and not garbled. No embedded instructions found.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Greedy tree search over draft/debug/improve/analyze beats one-shot. One-shot agents produced zero valid submissions on the LRA design tasks, so iteration and debugging are essential.
 number: 0 valid one-shot submissions of 960 runs (20 seeds x 8 agents); 12 greedy agents ran 720 runs
 setup: LRA (JAX/Flax), AIRA-dojo harness, 24 h or 500 steps per run, one H200, 10 seeds per greedy agent
 quote: "Notably, one-shot agents failed to produce any valid submissions. This confirms that single-turn code generation is insufficient for mechanistic design, and that iterative refinement, debugging, and validation are essential."
 where: p.13, sec 6.2.1
2. The agent's own validation score is a poor guide to the held-out score. The scorer is an isolated script with hidden test labels. In the Fig 3 example, validation was 0.3869 against test 0.5827, and a few nodes had equal val and test (0.3487).
 number: Val Acc 0.3869 vs Test Acc 0.5827 (Greedy GPT-5, 3-primitive MAD)
 setup: node-level values in Figure 3; the agent validates on a 70:30 split of the train set
 quote: "mA-mA-M-Mb-Mb-mA-Mb-M-Mb-Mb-mA-Mb-Mb-M-mA-Mb Val Acc: 0.3869, Test Acc: 0.5827"
 where: p.6, Fig 3. Method text, p.4-5: "independent evaluation script"; "ensuring test labels are hidden while the agent is building its solution".
3. Selecting the final answer from search is reasonably reliable. The gap between best-seen and submitted accuracy is small for most agents, with occasional large gaps.
 number: none (bar charts, Fig 11)
 quote: "Across all tasks, we observe generally small gaps, with submitted accuracy closely tracking best accuracy for most agents."
 where: p.15
4. Failure rate in an open-ended loop is high. Only a third of Autoresearch steps produced a valid score.
 number: 3,936 of 11,530 steps (34.1%)
 setup: 7 greedy agents x 10 seeds = 70 runs, Autoresearch, 5-minute training budget, one H200
 quote: "Across all runs, 3,936 out of 11,530 total steps (34.1%) yielded a valid numerical fitness value."
 where: p.16
5. Greedy full-file regeneration (minimal context on past explorations) gives compound edits and no causal attribution. Only 7 of 27 features were ever the sole change in an improvement step. Karpathy's persistent-session loop gives smaller but steadier gains.
 number: 156 improvement steps; 7 of 27 features ever changed solo
 setup: 100 Autoresearch runs, structural analysis of train.py (App. G)
 quote: "only 7 out of 27 features were ever the sole change in an improvement step, underscoring that agents predominantly make compound modifications."
 where: p.50 (App. G); also p.16 and p.19
6. Headline Autoresearch result: best BPB 0.968, surpassing the published reference. Caveats: it is the +Literature variant, a single best seed, and the baseline start differs from the original.
 number: 0.968 BPB (best seed, Opus 4.5 +Lit); baseline 1.0121 here vs 0.998 in the original
 setup: nanochat train.py, 5-minute budget, ClimbMix, H200 and sandbox with no internet vs H100 in the original; 10 seeds per agent
 quote: "Opus 4.5 +Literature achieves the single largest improvement in the table (∆ = 0.036) by introducing focal loss to replace cross-entropy around step 15."
 where: p.17, Table 5 (final BPB 0.968 in the +Lit column). The abstract and conclusion say "Greedy Opus 4.5" and omit +Lit.
7. Median performance is more modest than the headline. Medians sit near 0.99 against a baseline of 1.012. Literature access does not help uniformly.
 number: medians Opus 4.6 +Lit 0.990, Opus 4.6 0.991, Opus 4.5 0.992; CWM 1.012, OSS-120B 1.014
 quote: "Notably, adding literature access does not uniformly help: GPT-5 +Lit and Opus 4.5 +Lit underperform compared to their base variant, while Opus 4.6 +Lit slightly improves over Opus 4.6."
 where: p.16
8. A fraction of seeds beat the original Autoresearch gain.
 number: 20% of experiments beat a delta of 0.0205
 quote: "we could reproduce a delta with respect to baseline larger than that reported in Karpathy (2026) in 20%of the experiments."
 where: p.3 (intro); Fig 28 caption p.48 defines the criterion
9. AIRA-Compose finds hybrid architectures by probing a tiny fraction of the space (about 100-200 architectures per seed).
 number: 2,307 unique architectures = 3.17% of the 2-primitive space; 2,248 = 0.0052% of the 3-primitive space (170 runs)
 quote: "A total of 170 agentic runs yielded 2,248 unique architectures, probing 0.0052% of the search space."
 where: p.9 and p.11
10. At 1B and a fixed 37.5B-token budget, AIRAformer-D (Stretched) beats Llama 3.2 on loss and accuracy. Mean over 3 seeds; std is small but the margins are also small.
 number: val loss 2.734±.001 vs Llama 3.2 2.815±.003; 0-shot avg 59.7 vs 57.5; DCLM Core 48.9 vs 46.9
 quote: "AIRAformer-D Stretched achieves the lowest validation loss of 2.734, highest average 0-shot accuracy of 59.7% (60.8%) and highest DCLM Core score (48.9%)"
 where: p.10, Table 2
11. The hybrid results are weaker and single-seed. The best AIRAhybrid has the lowest loss, but the Composer-found baseline (2Mb-M-3A) has the best DCLM score. The abstract's claim of 54%/71%/23%/37% faster scaling appears only in the abstract. I found no body-text derivation. The body gives slope deltas instead.
 number: AIRAhybrid-D (Str.) loss 2.719 vs Nemotron-2 approx. 2.732; Composer 2.724; Composer DCLM 49.3 vs 48.5 for AIRAhybrid-D
 setup: single seed, 1B, 37.5B tokens, Nemotron approximated with MoE replaced by MLP
 quote: "Results are from a single seed."
 where: p.11, Table 3
12. Attention-heavy agent designs win on fixed tokens but lose on iso-compute.
 quote: "Attention-heavy AIRAformer-C and AIRAformer-D architectures achieve superior validation loss in the fixed-token-budget setting, as expected (Table 2), while balanced architectures are more compute-efficient in the isoFLOP regime."
 where: p.10
13. LRA agent designs recombine known methods. Best agents come within about 2-3pp of human SOTA on Text and Retrieval, and normalized scores are far below 1.
 number: NS 0.257±0.054 (ListOps, non-config, greedy, n=12); Text config 0.178±0.064
 quote: "they do not represent fundamentally novel contributions to the efficient attention literature."
 where: p.13-15. The 12 agents include 8 weak/non-SOTA models.
14. More freedom hurts weak agents. The configurable setup helped 4 greedy agents and hurt 7.
 number: 7 regressed, 4 improved; CWM -11.5pp, Devstral -10.8pp, Opus 4.6 +4.5pp
 quote: "Configurability produces mixed results across the 12 greedy agents: 7 regressed on average while 4 improved"
 where: p.15

LIMITS
- Variance: 10 seeds for greedy and 20 for one-shot. IsoToken results are 3 seeds for formers and 1 seed for hybrids. Autoresearch best-seed claims rest on a single seed out of 10. The Gemini agents show the largest seed variance.
- Baselines: Nemotron-H and Nemotron-2 are approximated at small scale. The Composer baseline uses a different search (6-layer small scale, stacked). The Autoresearch baseline starts at 1.012 here against 0.998 in the original, so the gap to the "published minimum" mixes hardware and setup differences.
- AIRA-Compose scored only 16-layer proxies on a single dataset per task. The aggregation (clustering) and extrapolation steps are non-agentic.
- The RSI framing is aspirational. The agents design models other than themselves, and no loop is closed.
- Authors concede the following (p.18-19): agents are limited to engineering-level synthesis; literature access is not uniformly useful; full-file regeneration prevents causal attribution; and the harness has no persistent state.
- Agent weakness is partly framework bias (PyTorch-trained models writing JAX/Flax) and OOM or numerical failures.
- Not shown: cost per result, ablation of the search policy (greedy vs MCTS), and any test of whether the discoveries transfer beyond 3B.
- Dated: the models named (Opus 4.5/4.6, Gemini 3/3.1, GPT-5) will age.

BUILDS ON
AIRS-Bench (Lupidi et al., 2026); AIRA-dojo (Toledo et al., 2025); AIRA_2 (Hambardzumyan et al., 2026), whose 70:30 validation split is reused; Composer (Acun et al., 2025); Autoresearch (Karpathy, 2026) and nanochat (Karpathy, 2025); Long Range Arena (Tay et al., 2020); MAD (Poli et al., 2024); recursive self-improvement (Good, 1966; Schmidhuber, 1987, 2003); the "march of 9s" (Karpathy and Patel, 2025).

CODE
- Operator definitions (p.4): Draft generates the initial candidates; Debug fixes execution or logical errors; Improve refines working solutions; Analyze reads the solution at each step. Greedy search drafts 5 solutions, applies improve to the highest-validation node, and applies debug when analyze flags a bug.
- Task layout (p.4): project_description.md, prepare.py and evaluate_prepare.py (hide test labels), evaluate.py (isolated scorer), metadata.yaml.
- Valid submission rate (Eq 1): VSR_{a,t} = V_{a,t} / T_{a,t}.
- Normalized score (Eq 2-3): NS = (phi(s) - phi(s_min)) / (phi(s_sota) - phi(s_min)), with phi(s) = -log10(|s - s_opt|); failed submissions score 0 (p.9).
- Full best train.py in App. H (pp.50-55). It is a long listing and not worth keeping.

FIGURES
- Fig 2/4 (p.5, 7): pipeline diagrams of problem, harness and solution space.
- Fig 3 (p.6): partial Greedy GPT-5 search tree with debug and improve edges, FAILED nodes, and val vs test accuracy. Best single picture of the draft/debug/improve loop and the val/test gap.
- Fig 9/10 (p.14): valid submission rate and normalized score per agent.
- Fig 11 (p.15): best vs submitted accuracy, the generalization gap.
- Fig 12/13 (p.16-18): Autoresearch per-seed BPB distributions and best-seed trajectories. Table 5 (p.17) gives step-by-step edits.
- Fig 28 (p.48): per-seed trajectories, with green marks for seeds beating 0.0205.
- Fig 5/6 (p.10-12): isoFLOP curves; Fig 7 is the latency/loss Pareto plot.

PLACEMENT
Marginal fit. It is an empirical case study of an agent search loop, not loop-engineering theory, and its pretraining results are off-topic. Usable material:
- Note 02 (loop shapes): the Draft/Debug/Improve/Analyze tree and greedy vs one-shot (claim 1). Use as a sharpens-style citation.
- Note 03 (scorekeeper): the isolated evaluate.py with hidden test labels, and the val vs test gap (claims 2, 3).
- Note 09 (failure modes): 34.1% valid steps, 0% one-shot validity, compound edits and attribution loss, and the headline caveats (claims 4, 5, 6, 7).
- Notes 05, 07 and 08: only a passing mention at most. The loop is a bounded run (24 h or 500 steps), so it adds little on long-running loops or the autonomy ladder, and it does not close a self-improvement loop.
Recommend a short citation row plus one or two sentences in 03 and 09, and a references row. Do not add new prose to 08.
